note: Intersections Diagnostics V1 rules. Values follow the agreed methodology (29 Oct 2026); items marked 'decision' were agreed in addition to it.
time_note: All data are stored in UTC. Inputs without an offset, 30-minute slots, weekdays, holidays and display use the region's local time; every query is sent in UTC.

q2.note: Per detector: >= min_vehicles over the 60 minutes passes even with missing 5-minute records; below it, FAIL needs all records, otherwise INSUFFICIENT DATA. A negative 5-minute count is not a valid count and is treated as missing ("missing"); "zero" counts it as 0, "keep" uses it as stored.
q2.tolerance_note: Decision with the methodology owner (5 Nov 2026): a site where only one active detector is below min_vehicles (with all its records) is screened instead of being a Detector Health Issue; two or more such detectors remain a Detector Health Issue. Missing records are unchanged (INSUFFICIENT DATA). 0 restores the strict gate.

q3.note: Methodology 9 as written: NORMAL when two measures are assessable and fewer than two are abnormal, even when the third (not assessable) could have made it ABNORMAL. true withholds that case as INSUFFICIENT DATA (Grey); for discussion, not the methodology.

alignment.note: Live feeds are written at a fixed offset from the grid (detector counts at :03/:08, PerfKpi/PerfApproach at :07/:22). An off-grid record of a feed in written_after_interval goes to the interval that ended before its stamp (floor); any other feed goes to the interval its stamp falls in (ceil). Within tolerance_seconds of a grid point a record is moved onto that point.
alignment.written_after_note: IntersectionPerfKpi and IntersectionPerfApproach records are written about 7 minutes after the quarter-hour they describe (15:07 = 14:45-15:00; confirmed with the data owner, Nov 2026), and SCATS detector counts about 3 minutes after their 5 minutes (15:03 = 14:55-15:00). They go to the interval that ended before the stamp, and the query reaches one interval past the period. The period's last records are written at about end + 3 min (detectors) and end + 7 min (PerfKpi/PerfApproach), hence data_latency_minutes 10.

tomtom.delay_note: Decision (3 Nov 2026, with the methodology owner): Q5 ranks the approaches by both TomTom control delay (IntersectionTurnKpi ControlDelaySec) and approach delay (ApproachDelaySec) (ranked_delays); a SCATS-identified approach agrees when it has the greatest of either delay or the longest queue. delay_metric is the delay written to the contract's single largest-delay field. Per approach and movement it is the plain mean of the stored 15-minute turn records, and a negative delay counts as 0, as in the chatbot's tomtom/los.py and delay_policy.py. Options: delay_metric "approach_delay"; delay_mean "sample_weighted"; negative_delay "keep".
tomtom.note: Methodology section 13: Q5 reports approach queue length and the largest queue from the TomTom Junction Analytics queue history (API archive). Needs TOMTOM_API_KEY; without it, or if the call fails, the queue is reported as unavailable and the rest of Q5 still runs.

link_speed.note: Methodology (speed addition): on an Amber or Red click, show the TomTom speed of the site's incoming (EGRESS) links for the same 30-minute period, and the historical reference speed: the same feed's speed in the same 30 minutes of the reference weeks (median, read on the click, not stored). Supplementary only: it never changes Q1, Q2, Q3, the Q5 agreement or the category. Missing speed is shown as unavailable. No network-wide speed screening and no speed baseline.

contract.note: Template registry IDs in the production contract. D001 is the contract's example; the D002 ID is a placeholder until the production team confirms it.
